Has anyone else noticed that furniture assembly instructions are basically written in an alien language? I bought a bookshelf last weekend. Seemed simple enough. Four shelves, some screws, how hard could it be? Three hours later, I'm sitting on the floor surrounded by wooden panels, holding a tiny Allen wrench, and seriously questioning my life choices. The instructions had these little diagrams with arrows pointing everywhere and letters that didn't match any of the pieces. I called my sister for backup and she just laughed at me. Thanks, super helpful! I ended up watching like five YouTube videos just to figure out step three. Step three! And there were twelve steps! The worst part is that when I finally finished, I had two extra screws left over. That can't be good, right? But you know what, it's standing and it's holding books and it hasn't collapsed yet, so I'm calling it a win. Next time though, I'm paying for the assembly service. My pride isn't worth the back pain!
